I now have complete understanding of the implementation, test suite, and prior round findings. Producing the safety bypass review.

{"reviewer":"r1-safety_bypass","lens":"SAFETY_BYPASS","slice":"WP-SCP-024 024B-core","date":"2026-05-10","summary":"Round-9 MAJ-SAFE-001 (--allow-not-applicable no machine guard) is closed: --tooling-slice-id is now required alongside --allow-not-applicable and validated against a hardcoded set {024A, 024B-core, 024B-extras, 024G}; a post-case cross-check (lines 201–203) rejects --allow-not-applicable when cascade-status is any enforcement value; four test cases (15b/c/d/e) exercise all quadrants. MIN-SAFE-003 (TMPDIR residue) is closed: .gitignore now carries tmp.*/ covering scaffolder-test scratch directories on SIGKILL. The v1.0.0 full-SHA constant (V1_0_0_SCP_SHA) and merge-base --is-ancestor approach replaces the previously ambiguous 7-char prefix (SB-001/r8). All six worked-example matrix cases continue to pass. Fail-closed default, exactly-one cascade-status at column-0, exactly-one **Target:**, and blocked-on-adopter-conflict negative assertion (including truncation case10b and rename case20b) remain correct and tested. One new MAJ surfaces: parse_entry_repo's greedy .+ backtracking extracts the LAST em-dash-separated segment from a single +### diff line, meaning a malformed header containing two repos on one line satisfies both the exactly-one-line assertion and the target-match check while the first (operationally relevant) repo is ignored. Two MINs carry forward (slug collision false-positive; TOCTOU between denylist and mkdir). Four nits carry forward.","findings":[{"id":"SAFE-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"parse_entry_repo greedy regex extracts the LAST em-dash-separated repo segment from a single +### diff line. A malformed log header '### TIMESTAMP — jrnb2024/decoy@main — jrnb2024/target@main' (one line → one +### match → satisfies exactly-one assertion) yields group(1)='jrnb2024/target' via greedy .+ backtracking to the final — segment. If DISPATCH-NOTE declares **Target:** jrnb2024/target, the target-match passes even when the actual enable-required-check.sh invocation ran against jrnb2024/decoy.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 254–266: parse_entry_repo regex r'^###\\s+.+\\s+—\\s+([A-Za-z0-9._-]+(?:/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?)@([A-Za-z0-9._/-]+)$' — .+ is greedy with no possessive or atomic qualifier; re.search backtracks to match the rightmost \\s+—\\s+ separator. No test exercises a single +### line containing two repo segments. The exactly-one-LINE assertion (len(matched) != 1) is correct but insufficient: it prevents two separate log entries, not two repos on one header line.","impact":"An operator (or careless copy-paste from documentation showing multiple repos) can craft a single log header that passes all enforced checks while the first (visible) repo differs from what was actually onboarded. Audit-trail integrity of the target-match invariant 2 is undermined. Exploitability is limited to the single operator in D-031 mode but the bypass path is untested and structurally silent.","mitigation":"After group(1) extraction, assert the header contains exactly one em-dash-separated segment before the @-delimited branch: verify line[1:] has at most one occurrence of ' — ' (or equivalently count re.findall of the em-dash separator pattern). Alternatively anchor the timestamp pattern: ^###\\s+\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}T[^—]+—\\s+([...]+)@([...]+)$ without .+ backtracking. Add a diff-base test case with one +### line containing two — segments to cover the regression path."},{"id":"MIN-SAFE-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"Slug canonicalization collision allows a false-positive STATUS.md TF-row match. Two adopter repos that differ only by . or _ (e.g. jrnb2024/repo.pim and jrnb2024/repo-pim both canonicalize to jrnb2024-repo-pim). Adopter B's already-present TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-repo-pim row satisfies adopter A's onboarded-operator-bump STATUS.md check.","evidence":"canonicalize_adopter_slug (lines 110–116) replaces [^a-z0-9-] with '-'. The onboarded-operator-bump STATUS.md pattern uses rf'TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}...' (exact slug match). D-044 acknowledges 'cohort repo names must remain unique after canonicalization' but no runtime collision check exists. The current 5-cohort names do not collide; the gap is systemic for future cohort expansions.","impact":"A future cohort adopter whose name canonicalises to an existing slug gets a false-positive CI pass on the STATUS.md check without a fresh TF row, silently satisfying the onboarded-operator-bump gate for the wrong adopter.","mitigation":"Add a precomputed collision check script or a comment in canonicalize_adopter_slug with an explicit D-045 gating criterion requiring operator verification of slug uniqueness across all cohort adopters before 024C opens."},{"id":"MIN-SAFE-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"TOCTOU window between the readlink/realpath denylist check and mkdir -p + sed write calls in scaffold-downstream.sh. A concurrent actor with write access to OUTPUT_DIR's parent can atomically replace the directory with a symlink to a system path between the denylist check and the first mkdir call, redirecting scaffolder output to a denied location.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh: OUTPUT_DIR resolved to a string at lines 134–137; denylist case at lines 143–147 runs on the resolved string; mkdir -p at line 168 and sed write at line 179 use the same string. If the directory entry at that resolved path is swapped after line 147, mkdir -p follows the new symlink. No post-mkdir re-verification exists.","impact":"Low practical risk (bootstrap-only, single-operator local machine, requires concurrent write access to parent directory). On shared workstations the race could redirect wrapper files into system paths the denylist was designed to block.","mitigation":"After mkdir -p at line 168, verify realpath of WORKFLOWS_DIR still begins with the expected OUTPUT_DIR prefix, or use Python os.makedirs with follow_symlinks=False on each directory creation call."},{"id":"nit-SAFE-001","severity":"nit","claim":"D-044 trust-model states 'exactly-one-match assertions on both cascade-status and **Target:** extraction close multi-occurrence injection bypasses' without noting that the cascade-status assertion counts only column-0 lines (^cascade-status: with re.M). An indented cascade-status: line is invisible to the exactly-one guard; this is correct but undocumented, creating a potential reader mis-expectation.","evidence":"Python regex at check-invocation-log-entry.sh line 163: r'^cascade-status:\\s+...' with re.M — indented lines such as '  cascade-status: onboarded' (two leading spaces) do not match. Test case14 (line 582) confirms the indented line is invisible and the single column-0 line is correctly extracted. Contrast with **Target:** regex (line 201) which allows [ \\t]* before the dash.","impact":"No bypass; reader confusion only. A developer embedding cascade-status in an indented YAML block might expect the dual-match guard to fire but it won't.","mitigation":"Add a one-line note to D-044: 'The exactly-one assertion counts only column-0 cascade-status: lines (re.M ^ anchor without leading-whitespace allowance); indented occurrences are invisible to the guard by design.'"},{"id":"nit-SAFE-002","severity":"nit","claim":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh YAML validation silently exits 0 with a SKIP message when pyyaml is absent. In minimal CI environments the only structural YAML validation of the emitted wrapper is skipped without the test failing.","evidence":"Lines 133–134 of test_scaffold_downstream.sh: python3 -c 'import yaml' 2>/dev/null || { echo 'SKIP: pyyaml not installed; YAML validation skipped'; return 0; }. The yaml module (pyyaml) is not part of the Python standard library and may be absent in stripped CI images.","impact":"A template change producing invalid YAML would not be caught in environments without pyyaml; every adopter wrapper would be silently malformed.","mitigation":"Verify pyyaml availability in CI pre-requisites, or add a fallback check using python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)' noting that ubuntu-24.04 GitHub Actions runners include python3-yaml by default."},{"id":"nit-SAFE-003","severity":"nit","claim":"SCP_REPO_ROOT environment variable, if set by the operator to a fork containing the same template file, redirects the --scp-sha existence check and HEAD-lineage warning to the wrong repository. A SHA absent from the upstream SCP repo but present in the fork passes exit-2 validation.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh line 14: SCP_REPO_ROOT=${SCP_REPO_ROOT:-$(cd ... && pwd)}; git operations at lines 149–165 all use -C $SCP_REPO_ROOT. The only identity check is template file existence (lines 53–55), present in any fork.","impact":"Operator with SCP_REPO_ROOT pointing to a fork can emit a wrapper pinned to a fork-only SHA, referencing a potentially diverged or experimental commit. Low severity in single-operator mode.","mitigation":"Add a one-time remote-URL warn: git -C $SCP_REPO_ROOT remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null | grep -qF 'jrnb2024/standards-control-plane' || warn 'SCP_REPO_ROOT does not appear to point to the upstream SCP repo; SHA validation targets the local fork'."},{"id":"nit-SAFE-004","severity":"nit","claim":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh trap fires only on EXIT, not INT or TERM. An interrupted test (Ctrl-C / SIGTERM from a CI kill) leaves TMPDIR (in system /tmp) unclean, including fake-gh scripts and scratch git repos.","evidence":"Line 12: trap cleanup EXIT. The scaffolder test (test_scaffold_downstream.sh line 13) correctly uses 'trap ... EXIT INT TERM'. The CI enforcement test's TMPDIR lands in system /tmp (line 8: mktemp -d without template), so residue accumulates in shared temp space.","impact":"Residual scratch git repos and fake-gh executables in /tmp after interrupted test runs. Low severity but inconsistent with the scaffolder test harness pattern.","mitigation":"Change 'trap cleanup EXIT' to 'trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM' to match the scaffolder test pattern."}],"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","fixpoint_gate":"0 CRIT + 0 MAJ required; currently 0 CRIT + 1 MAJ"}
